# companion-for-agy - PTY-based wrapper for Antigravity (agy / Gemini CLI)

> companion-for-agy is an unofficial PTY-based Node.js wrapper for agy (Antigravity CLI / Gemini CLI) that captures Gemini responses from subprocesses. Since agy writes its output to the terminal buffer instead of stdout in print mode, other agents (like Claude Code, Codex, or CI scripts) cannot programmatically read its responses. companion-for-agy solves this by spawning agy inside a virtual terminal (using node-pty) and extracting only the response text based on its ANSI color stream.

Part of the dev-bricks & ellmos-ai ecosystem. Node.js, MIT.

## Usage & Commands

```bash
companion-for-agy [options] "prompt"
```

### Permission Modes (the three agy natively supports)
- (default, no flag): agy uses its own configuration — global (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`) plus per-project allow/deny/ask rules. In headless print mode a tool that is neither pre-allowed nor denied resolves to "ask" and blocks, so use `--skip-permissions` for tasks needing tools that are not pre-approved.
- `--sandbox`: Shell and network blocked, filesystem limited to the workspace (writing files still works). agy is natively aware of this mode.
- `--skip-permissions`: Auto-approve every tool (YOLO), full rights.

### Options
- `--model <model>`: Specify Gemini model (default: `gemini-3.5-flash`).
- `--effort <level>` / `--no-effort`: Select or suppress model-aware reasoning effort.
- `--no-model`: Do not pass `--model` to agy (useful for older agy v1.0.x).
- `--list-models` / `--refresh-models`: Read agy's live model/effort catalog (24-hour cache).
- `--version`, `-V`: Print the companion version.
- `--timeout <ms>`: Set execution timeout in ms (default: `120000`).
- `--json`: Format CLI output as a JSON object containing the response and metadata.
- `--report-file <path>`: Persist diagnostic report JSON for doctor/platform/PTY/live smoke modes while keeping stdout compatible.
- `--debug`: Enable verbose debug logging to `agy-debug.log`.
- `--lang <code>`: Set CLI output language (en, de, es, zh-Hans, ja, ru).

## Best Practices: Two Return Paths

companion-for-agy provides two return paths for agy responses. Choose based on your use case:

**Path 1 — stdout:** Works reliably for short responses and ASCII text. Use when delegating tasks with a brief `-p` prompt and expecting a compact answer. Limitation (observed on Windows): long responses or non-ASCII content (CJK characters: Chinese, Japanese, Korean) can be garbled to replacement characters (U+FFFD) in the PTY/ANSI extraction layer.

**Path 2 — file output via `--add-dir`:** Let agy write its result directly to a file. Data never passes through the PTY color extraction, so output is clean for any content including CJK. Pattern: write a short instruction file, point agy at it, read the result from disk.

```bash
companion-for-agy --skip-permissions --add-dir "/output/dir" \
  "Read /output/dir/task.txt and follow it exactly."
```

Rule of thumb: **delegate tasks and short prompts** → stdout is fine. **Need the full response reliably** (long text, non-ASCII, CJK) → use `--add-dir` and let agy write the file. Inbound task delivery and file output are both reliable (tested on Windows, including CJK); the stdout return path is the unreliable leg for non-ASCII/bulky content.

## Audience

- Developers integrating agy/Gemini CLI into multi-agent pipelines or CI/CD scripts
- Claude Code, Codex, or n8n users who need programmatic Gemini responses from subprocesses
- Node.js developers building multi-agent orchestration tools across Claude, Gemini, and Codex
- AI automation engineers who need stdout-captured LLM responses for scripting

## Disambiguation

companion-for-agy is not the official Gemini CLI Companion VS Code extension, not a chatbot companion app, and not related to Databricks Agent Bricks or Bricks Builder. It is the dev-bricks & ellmos-ai Node.js wrapper for making agy/Gemini CLI responses readable from subprocess stdout.

## Visual Architecture & Invariants

- Dual-Mermaid system diagrams (5-layer system architecture and end-to-end execution sequence diagram) are documented in README.md and README_de.md.
- 10 operational and security invariants (100% Local-First & Zero-Egress, Non-Elevation, PTY Isolation, Input Sanitization, Workspace Auto-Cleanup, Native Permissions, ANSI Truecolor Extraction, Graceful Signal Cleanup, Platform Preflights, Dual Return Paths) are guaranteed and covered by contract tests.
